title: POC Weekly: Queue Spikes & Throttle Hunt

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (Apex Platform), Ananya Gupta (Apex ML), Leila Torres (Apex SRE), Priyam Das (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick follow-up from incident windows last week; focus on queue tail lat and throttling behavior.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh quick agenda — recap last week's 5xx windows, dig into traces Samira prepared, and agree instrumentation + next steps.
00:22 Marcus: yeah thanks, Jordan. we saw three pretty nasty spikes during peak catalog ingest, maybe between 10:18 and 10:42 last Thursday. lat spiked, then a bunch of 502/503s, not sure if it was network or your runtime.
00:37 Samira: ok, uh we looked at the partial traces you sent. one pattern is queue growth on the serving side, like requests pile up and then we hit tenant throttling which kills a chunk and returns 502-ish. sometimes it's a 503, sometimes 500, per the transcriber — it's messy.
00:55 Ananya: and for us the concern is not just the 5xx but the long tail — some user calls are 10s, which breaks our front-end timeouts. we tightened client timeouts to 6s as a temporary mitigation but that's not ideal.
01:12 Jordan: right — so first hypothesis: burst causes KV/prefix cache misses, causing deserialization work and CPU pressure then queueing. second hypothesis: our tenant-level rate limiter kicks in on aggregated concurrency, causing early drop. both could coexist.
01:36 Leila: i can add that our infra metrics didn't show NLB saturation but we did see a small bump in retransmit rates, maybe unrelated.
01:50 Samira: quick note — in the traces i saw some calls to, uh, Llama-3 like models, sorry mis-said, we mean 'Llama3' variants and one to Mistal v2 — which have very different tokenization sizes; that makes request-cost vary.
02:08 Marcus: yeah, we have mixed models. some routes call the long sequence summarizer which is heavy.
02:20 Jordan: ok, let's walk through a sample trace (Samira shared a replay link in the meeting chat).
02:28 Samira: i pulled the replay for the 10:30 spike — so at 10:30:12 we see a sudden burst: 120 req/sec sustained for 18s, then queue depth jumps, KV cache miss rate goes from 8% to 61%. that correlates with 502s at the client.
02:52 Ananya: can we get that exact trace id?
02:55 Samira: yeah trace id is rdin-20261112-3312, link: https://redwood.example/trace/rdin-20261112-3312 (shared in chat).
03:05 Marcus: when you say KV cache miss — is that prefix cache or full KV?
03:10 Samira: mostly prefix cache, the runtime logs show prefix_cache.miss spike. it's the warmup storm: many new prefixes because the burst contains a bunch of new session prefixes.
03:24 Jordan: common POC note — lots of small, unique prefixes cause cache churn and a cascade. we recommend enabled prefix caching plus sampling pre-warm for heavy routes.
03:40 Leila: in terms of throttling, our metrics show token rate thresholds per tenant were exceeded and the rate limiter dropped some requests; do you have a knob for per-route vs per-tenant?
03:53 Samira: yes, there's tenant-level and route-level. by default POC tenants are on shared rate policies; we can configure route isolation for your heavy pipelines so they don't affect other routes.
04:06 Priyam: what's the lift to put that in place in our demo/dedicated env?
04:10 Samira: small config change — we can apply a route-level policy and do a quick canary with 5% of traffic to start.
04:18 Jordan: another immediate mitigation is client-side retries with jittered exponential backoff and a retry budget, that should reduce demand spikes. but don't over-retry because that amplifies pressure.
04:33 Marcus: so recommended backoff values?
04:36 Jordan: start with base 150ms, multiply 2x, cap at 2s, max attempts 3, and include jitter. that's conservative.
04:45 Ananya: we already had 5 attempts default in the SDK, so that might be making things worse.
04:50 Leila: yeah that explains amplification.
04:55 Samira: i also noticed some request payloads that include large context blobs — if those are unnecessary you can truncate client-side. that reduces work per request.
05:08 Marcus: is there a way to see per-request token counts on the console?
05:13 Samira: yes Redwood Console (the slow one? transcribed as 'Redwood Consul' earlier in notes) shows token histograms per route — we can open a filtered view for the three windows.
05:25 Jordan: quick check — do we want to run a controlled burst against the Dedicated pool or try toggling prefix caching first?
05:32 Priyam: let's do both: first toggle cache off/on in a small canary to reproduce, then run a replay burst against Dedicated stage.
05:41 Marcus: ok timing?
05:43 Jordan: we'd like logs and a replay run by Tuesday 11/24, so we can do a deep-dive on 11/25. Samira can provide the debug instructions.
05:52 Samira: i'll attach the commands — sample curl commands and the sample replay harness (link) — in the thread after the call.
06:00 Marcus: can you also annotate which requests were kernel-bound vs I/O bound in the logs?
06:06 Samira: we'll flag the span kind in the traces. sometimes the auto-annotation misses kernel vs user-time, but we'll add extra tags.
06:16 Leila: note — our security team asked about log retention and pii redaction if you need request bodies. is there a mechanism to redact before sharing?
06:25 Jordan: yes we have a redaction pipeline and can provide a sanitized dump. i'll include the security snippet and the SOC2 pointer.
06:32 Priyam: do we anticipate needing Dedicated-only migration to avoid multi-tenant throttles?
06:37 Samira: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbors but if your workload has bursty new prefixes you'll still hit cache warmup; Dedicated just gives you predictable throughput and avoids shared tenant rate-level interference.
06:49 Ananya: one more thing — we saw occasional 504s labeled as gateway timeouts; any idea where those come from?
06:54 Samira: 504s usually mean upstream didn't respond before the NGINX/Gateway timed out; could be long model compute or stuck requests. traces will show whether compute is blocked.
07:05 Jordan: step-by-step proposal: 1) Samira collects full traces and compressed logs for the three windows; 2) Apex runs a controlled replay with 120 req/s for 25s against dedicated stage with prefix-caching toggled; 3) both teams compare token histograms, kv miss rate, queue depth curves; 4) tune client retry to 3 attempts with jitter; 5) do canary route isolation if needed.
07:32 Marcus: ok agreed.
07:36 (brief crosstalk)
07:45 Samira: small gotcha — when you toggle prefix cache off it might reduce memory pressure but increase compute per request so watch latency.
07:58 Leila: that's fine, we'll monitor during the tests.
08:05 Jordan: also i flagged an internal infra ticket to look for kernel selection anomalies; sometimes the runtime picks a suboptimal kernel variant under short sequences causing CPU spikes. Samira is cc'd.
08:19 Samira: yes, i logged that as INF-6123.
08:23 Ananya: will you share the replay harness?
08:25 Samira: link: https://s3.apex/replay-harness (will upload sanitized input).
08:30 Marcus: do you have a recommended sample size for the bursts? 120 req/s felt real but we can try multiple intensities.
08:36 Samira: try 60, 120, and 240 for short windows (15, 25, 10s) to understand threshold shapes.
08:44 Jordan: one more ask — if the burst reproduces, capture p95,p99 CPU and queue depth and also the rate limiter counters. those are the key triage signals.
08:56 Leila: noted.
09:01 Priyam: ok timeline check: Samira artifacts by 11/23, Apex runs tests 11/24, deep-dive 11/25. can we schedule the 11/25 now?
09:09 Jordan: i'll send a calendar invite for 11/25 10:00 PT.
09:12 Marcus: thanks. small FYI — meanwhile we're going to flip client retries to 3 attempts to reduce amplification, we'll document results.
09:20 Samira: excellent.
09:24 Jordan: any blockers on security or compliance for us getting sanitized logs?
09:28 Leila: we'll need the redaction snippet, if it's automated that's best.
09:32 Jordan: i'll include it after the call.
09:36 (silence, wrap up)
09:40 Jordan: ok, to recap: Samira sends traces+replay instructions+curl examples+security snippet; Apex runs controlled bursts and shares results; we meet 11/25 for deep dive. I'll follow up with a short runbook and recommended client config. Thanks everyone.
09:57 Priyam: thanks all.
10:00 Meeting ends.
